subject: Business Models
title: Circular Fashion
description: A quick, practical guide to Circular Fashion.

hook.text: The fashion industry produces 100 billion garments/year. 87% end up in landfills. Circular fashion rethinks this.

buildup.text: Circular fashion designs clothes for longevity, resale, rental, and recycling instead of single-season disposal.

discovery.text: ThredUp, The RealReal, and Rent the Runway built billion-dollar businesses around secondhand and rental fashion.

twist.text: Fast fashion brands sell 'sustainable' lines while producing billions of disposable garments. Greenwashing is rampant.

climax.text: True circular fashion requires systemic change: materials, design, business models, and consumer behavior all together.

punchline.text: 100B garments, 87% in landfills. Circular fashion is the model that must win.

quiz.question: What percentage of garments end up in landfills?

details.summary: Circular fashion redesigns the clothing industry around reuse, repair, rental, and recycling rather than the take-make-dispose model. Brands like Patagonia, ThredUp, and The RealReal are building businesses around extending garment lifespans and recapturing material value at end of use.
details.whyItMatters: The fashion industry produces 10% of global carbon emissions and generates 92 million tons of textile waste annually..
takeaways: Garments are designed for reuse, repair, and recycling rather than disposal
Resale and rental models generate multiple revenue streams per garment
The circular fashion market is growing at 15-20% annually

faq.question: How do circular fashion businesses generate revenue?
faq.answer: Resale platforms like ThredUp take commissions on secondhand sales. Rental subscriptions like Rent the Runway charge monthly fees for rotating wardrobes. Brands like Patagonia sell reconditioned used items. Recycling companies sell recovered textile fibers to manufacturers for new garments.

faq.question: Can circular fashion become mainstream or will it remain niche?
faq.answer: The resale market is projected to reach 350 billion globally by 2027. Luxury resale is already widely accepted. Fast fashion economics face regulatory pressure from textile waste legislation in the EU. Rising consumer awareness and improving logistics are driving mainstream adoption rapidly.
